cases.summary: Flag updates written as independent if-statements: a simultaneous read and write at occupancy 1 sets empty.
Reset does not clear the registered full flag.
full is computed from the current write pointer instead of the next one.
The storage array is declared one entry short, so the last slot is lost at wraparound.
Two bugs: full asserts one word early, and reset does not clear the read pointer.
Two bugs: empty ignores the wrap bit, and a read while empty is not ignored.
full ignores the wrap bit, so it is also asserted when the FIFO is empty.
Reads return the slot after the head.

briefs.text: A 4-entry byte FIFO for a sensor hub. To give the producer a cycle of warning, full should go high one entry early, when three bytes are stored, and further writes should then be refused.
A 4-deep FIFO feeding a decoder. The oldest byte should already be sitting on dout whenever the FIFO is not empty, so the decoder can look at it before deciding to pop it with rd_en.
A 2-entry command FIFO. If reset and a write arrive on the same edge, the command being written should be kept so that nothing is lost during a soft reset.
A 4-byte FIFO. A read requested while it is empty should not be dropped: the FIFO should remember it and deliver the next byte that arrives on dout as soon as it is written.
A 4-byte FIFO for a UART transmitter. The CPU checks full before writing, but if it writes anyway while full, the byte is silently discarded and the queue is unchanged.
A 2-entry FIFO. After reset it is empty, and asserting reset in the middle of operation throws away whatever was stored, even if a read or write was requested on that edge.

A 4-deep byte FIFO. When the consumer reads while the producer writes and the FIFO already holds some data, both happen. When it is completely full, a simultaneous write is refused and only the read happens.
A 4-entry byte FIFO with a registered output: after a successful read, dout holds the byte that was removed, and it keeps that value until the next successful read.
